title: KV cache tessellation manager and microfracture analytics
creator: Ravi Kapoor
description:
Problem statement:
Current KV cache allocation is increasingly fragmented for mixed-length workloads (chat + long-context) which causes high eviction churn and elevated kernel work during live batches. Existing slab/slot heuristics reduce average fragmentation but still leave long tail pockets that blow out token-serving latency during bursts.

Proposal summary:
Introduce a tessellation-based KV pool manager that partitions GPU KV memory into adaptive tiles (tessels) sized by observed token-cluster footprints. Each tessel maintains a lightweight occupancy signature (microfracture hash) to surface early fragmentation signals. The manager performs three coordinated actions:
  1) proactive tile consolidation during low-load micro-windows (opportunistic rewrite within same-GPU, zero-copy where possible),
  2) tile-aware allocation (prefer contiguous slots within low-entropy tessels),
  3) microfracture analytics that emits fragmentation scores (per-tessel and global) to guide runtime batch routing and evictions.

Why this approach?:
  - Tessellation matches observed spatial locality: many KV entries are short-lived and clustered by prompt/session, so adaptive tile sizing reduces internal fragmentation.
  - Microfracture signatures are small (<= 64B per tessel) and cheap to update per insertion/eviction, enabling near-real-time fragmentation telemetry without scanning pools.
  - Opportunistic consolidation piggybacks on low-util micro-batches to rewrite entries with minimal impact to latency SLOs.

Trade-offs considered:
  - Extra metadata per tessel increases memory overhead (~0.5-2% depending on tile granularity). Acceptable given projected reduction in churn.
  - Consolidation costs introduce GPU cycles; mitigated by strict budgeted windows and backpressure from latency hooks.
  - Consistency: cross-worker migration avoided for MVP; consolidation limited to local GPU memory to avoid networked copy complexity.

Implementation plan (high level):
  - Phase 1 (prototype): in-runtime feature-flagged module that creates tessels at pool init and computes microfracture signatures on ops. Expose metrics + admin API. (owner: Maya)
  - Phase 2 (schedulers/telemetry): feed per-tessel fragmentation into batch router to prefer low-frag GPUs for latency-sensitive requests. Add Grafana dashboard + alerts. (owner: Ravi)
  - Phase 3 (consolidation): implement opportunistic rewrite controller with safe preemption and epoch markers. Add tests and canary rollout.

Artifacts and links:
  - Design doc: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/KV+Tessellation+Design
  - Prototype PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/8342
  - Telemetry dashboard: https://grafana.redwood.ai/d/kv-frag/kv-fragmentation
acceptance_criteria:
1) Prototype emits per-tessel fragmentation metric for every active GPU and is visible in Grafana.
2) End-to-end microbench: mixed chat + long-context profile shows >=30% reduction in eviction churn and <=2% additional memory overhead.
3) Batch router uses fragmentation score to reduce high-latency tail requests by >=20% on canary.
4) Consolidation logic runs in budgeted windows and can be toggled off remotely without state corruption.
5) Unit + integration tests cover tessel boundary conditions, signature correctness, and preemption behavior.
comments: 2026-03-01 - Ravi Kapoor: Kickoff meeting today. Agreed on tessellation concept and microfracture signature format. Decided to avoid cross-GPU migration for MVP. Action: Maya to prototype signature updates in runtime insert/evict hot paths.

2026-03-03 - Maya Chen: Spike completed. Microfracture sig implemented as 64-bit xor-rolling fingerprint stored per tessel; update cost measured at ~12ns per op on our perf-runner. Created PR #8342 with initial tessel allocator and metrics emision. See PR for microbench results.

2026-03-04 - Philip Huang (review): Reviewed PR. Left feedback re: optimistic locking on tessel metadata and potential hot-writer contention. Suggested per-thread scratch buffer to batch metadata writes. Also requested a safety valve to disable consolidation when GPUUtil > 75%.

2026-03-05 - Maya Chen: Addressed locking feedback by switching to atomic-free rendezvous using epoch counters and batched CAS updates. Added take-down switch when latency tail > configured SLO. Updated PR and added unit tests for rare race cases.

2026-03-06 - Ravi Kapoor: Running canary on infra-staging with 3 GPUs. Early telemetry: global fragmentation score dropped 34% on mixed workload and eviction churn down 28%. Next: formalize consolidation windows and add batch-router integration.
